title: The email opens with the contact's name, invoice-style signature, call to call
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in with Create and edit customers, on the build under test. The Maintenance Reminders feature is on (maintenance_reminders flag).
  2. A customer whose 'Send preventive maintenance notifications' setting is ON, with an asset that has a preferred contact carrying an email address (e.g. customer 'ZZAUTOTEST Fleet Co', unit 'Truck 12', contact 'Dave Brabay').
  3. The asset has one or more services currently inside their reminder window. Open the asset's contact card.
custom_steps:
1. Send a reminder and read the opening line, the signature and the call to action.
  2. On a location with no telephone, confirm the call to action is omitted.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • The email opens with the chosen contact's first and last name (for example 'Hi Dave Brabay').
  • The signature is the one the invoice email carries: Best regards, the user's name, the organization's name and the telephone of the location chosen in the header; the call to action is to call.
  • Where the location has no telephone, the call to action is omitted rather than printed with nothing after it.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-3780 (Maintenance Reminders); story SV-10575 (S19, The customer reminder email (sent by hand)); Chunk 2 MR spec (Confluence 897679389), Part 2 / S19; read 2 Oct 2026. Source-verified 2 October 2026; not yet build-verified.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S19-R19: “The email opens with the chosen contact's first and last name, for example Hi Dave Brabay. The signature is the one the invoice email already carries: Best regards, the user's name, the organization's name and the telephone of the location chosen in the header. The call to action is to call. Booking is a conversation, and a telephone is present where an email address often is not”
  • S19-R21: “Where the location has no telephone, the call to action is omitted rather than printed with nothing after it”
